label: input token t during the original phase
explanation: Token detector: fires whenever the input is the letter t during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at any position and any L. Precision 1.0 on dev; essentially silent on every other token, on the delimiter, and on copy-phase steps (only ~98 copy-phase activations, all at recall_idx 1, i.e. when t is fed back as input). Magnitude is highest (near max) when t is the first token of the sequence and drops for later positions (around 0.6-0.9 of max). It is weaker again when t has already appeared earlier in the sequence: a second t gets about 0.3-0.7 of max, and 93% of activation mass comes from first occurrences.

issues: Small imprecision: t at late positions with no earlier t can drop to about 0.48-0.64 of max (e.g. 'c l r b j f [t:0.48]' and 'r z z c 3 [t:0.64]'), so 'about 0.6-0.9 of max for later positions' understates how far it falls. This is a magnitude detail and does not affect the label.

Copy-phase activations (73 on test, 98 on dev) are all at recall_idx 1, are tiny (0.00-0.04 of max) and carry 0.0% of the mass. Each one follows a sequence that starts with t, which matches the explanation. This is noise, not a systematic class.

Test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.9993, F1 0.9997, mass recall 0.99999, and 0 false positives. The repetition effect also checks out: restricting to first occurrences gives mass recall 0.925, consistent with the reported ~93% of mass coming from first occurrences.
